data.title: Dynamics of mTORC1 activation in response to amino acids
data.authors: Manifava M; Ktistakis NT et al.

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.model_system: HEK293 cells; live imaging of RAPTOR and a fluorescent di-leucine analogue
data.finding: Live imaging shows mTORC1 moves to lysosomes within 2 minutes of amino acid addition and peaks by 5 minutes, in step with leucine arriving in lysosomes; phosphorylation of classic mTORC1 targets lags behind, suggesting mTORC1 passes briefly through the lysosome before acting on substrates elsewhere.
data.abstract_excerpt: Amino acids are essential activators of mTORC1 via a complex containing RAG GTPases, RAGULATOR and the vacuolar ATPase. Sensing of amino acids causes translocation of mTORC1 to lysosomes, an obligate step for activation. To examine the spatial and temporal dynamics of this translocation, we used live imaging of the mTORC1 component RAPTOR and a cell permeant fluorescent analogue of di-leucine methyl ester. Translocation to lysosomes is a transient event, occurring within 2 min of aa addition and peaking within 5 min.

extracted_findings.effect: mTORC1 lysosomal translocation is transient (2-5 min) and precedes target phosphorylation
